Travis Grigla was taken to St. John's Medical Center in Longview, Washington, where he was medically cleared and taken back to Portland by a federal agent. Cowlitz County charged Travis with possession of a stolen vehicle, unlawful possession of a firearm, possessing stolen firearms, both in reference to the firearms located in the stolen HSI vehicle. felony alluding, and violating community custody. However, that case remains open as Travis was charged in federal court with possession of child pornography, distribution of child pornography, and theft of government property. According to federal court documents, during the initial search of Travis' bedroom, an HSI agent discovered a black Samsung cell phone, which Travis was prohibited from possessing as a stipulation of his supervised release, stemming from his 2008 conviction of possessing and distributing child pornography. A search of the phone yielded photographs of Travis's paystubs and selfie photos of Travis, establishing that the phone was his, along with two videos depicting child pornography. Additionally, another phone known to be Travis's was recovered in a boot in the back of a task force officer's police car who had recovered the boots from the crashed HSI vehicle. A review of the SD card yielded hundreds of images of child pornography. Travis pleaded guilty and was given nearly 22 years in federal prison and upon completion of his sentence will be on supervised release for the rest of his life. He was also ordered to pay the United States government over $27,000 in restitution. Travis is currently serving his sentence at Terminal Island Federal Correctional Institution in Los Angeles and is scheduled for release in October October 242. event_summary.short: Registered sex offender carjacks federal agent's vehicle during search warrant execution, leads multi-agency pursuit from Oregon to Washington.

evidence.quote: Cowlitz County charged Travis with possession of a stolen vehicle, unlawful possession of a firearm, possessing stolen firearms, felony eluding, and violating community custody.
